# Release Notes

Simplyblock regularly provides new releases with new features, performance enhancements, bugfixes, and more.

This section provides detailed information about each simplyblock release, including new features, enhancements, bug
fixes, and known issues. Stay informed about the latest developments to ensure optimal performance and take full
advantage of simplyblock's capabilities.

---

<!-- source: https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/release-notes/26-4/ -->

# 26.4

Simplyblock is happy to release Simplyblock 26.4. The changes are grouped by the component they belong to: the
simplyblock control plane and storage plane, and the Kubernetes components, meaning the Simplyblock Operator and
Simplyblock CSI.

!!! warning "Draft"
    This page is a work in progress. Only the important changes of the operator API are collected so far. The
    control plane and storage plane entries, the operator and CSI driver features, the upgrade path, and the known
    issues are not final yet.

## Simplyblock

The control plane and the storage plane are released together and share a version number. The changes below apply
to every deployment, including a Kubernetes-based one.

### New Features

- **Control Plane:** Added secondary indices to the control plane's FoundationDB store. A lookup by anything other
  than the record id, such as the volumes of a storage pool or the node a device sits in, is answered from an index
  instead of a scan of the whole record class, so the cost of a lookup no longer grows with the size of the
  cluster. The indices of an upgraded cluster are backfilled by `sbctl cluster upgrade-complete`, and until
  an index is complete its reads fall back to a scan.
- **Control Plane:** Added `sbctl cluster build-indices`, `sbctl cluster check-indices`, and
  `sbctl cluster index-state` to operate those indices. The backfill is idempotent and safe to run against
  a live cluster, `check-indices` writes back what it can derive with `--repair`, and `index-state` lists where
  every index stands and takes a single one out of service with `--set disabled`.
- **Control Plane:** TODO, to be collected from the `sbcli` changes since 26.3.

### Fixes

- **Control Plane:** TODO, to be collected from the `sbcli` changes since 26.3.

## Kubernetes

The changes below apply to a Kubernetes-based deployment and ship with the Simplyblock Operator and
Simplyblock CSI.

### New Features

- **Operator:** TODO, to be collected from the `simplyblock-operator` changes since 26.3.

### Fixes

- **Operator:** TODO, to be collected from the `simplyblock-operator` changes since 26.3.

## Important Changes

The operator API moves from `storage.simplyblock.io/v1alpha1` to `storage.simplyblock.io/v1alpha2`. Every kind is
served at the new version, which is also the storage version, and a conversion webhook translates an existing
`v1alpha1` object so that a manifest written for 26.3 keeps working. The replication kinds are the exception and
stay at `v1alpha1`.

- Imperative operations are separate resources instead of fields on the entity they act on. Setting
  `StorageCluster.spec.action` is replaced by creating a `StorageClusterOps`, and the operation runs to a terminal
  phase and stays afterward as the record of what was done. `StorageClusterOps`, `StorageNodeOps`,
  `StorageDeviceOps`, `StoragePoolOps`, `PersistentVolumeOps`, `StorageBackupOps`, `ControlPlaneOps`, and
  `OperatorOps` share that shape, including `spec.abort` and the `Aborted` phase.
- A storage cluster is deployed from a `ClusterDeploymentConfig`. The operator inspects the workers, writes the
  draft, and an administrator approves it with `spec.approved`, after which the document is expanded into the
  `StorageCluster` and its `StorageNode` objects. The document is immutable once approved.
- A namespace holds at most one `StorageCluster`. A second storage cluster needs a namespace of its own.
- Every enum value of the group is PascalCase. An action such as `restart` is written `Restart`, and a phase such
  as `Completed` is written `Succeeded`.
- The status of a running operation is a state machine snapshot in `status.step`, replacing `status.subPhase`.
  `status.step.state` carries the step, and `status.step.deadline` is when that step expires.
- The annotation and label keys move from the `simplyblock.io/` prefix to `storage.simplyblock.io/`. Every spelling
  is read and the new one is written, so nothing has to be relabeled. The exception is
  `simplyblock.io/pod-affinity`, which has no prefixed spelling yet.
- The `StorageCluster` finalizer is renamed from `storage.simplyblock.io/cluster-finalizer` to
  `storage.simplyblock.io/storagecluster-finalizer`. The old key is read for one release.

### Renamed and Retired Resources

A kind that is absorbed is not converted. The upgrade constructs the successor, and a manifest that creates the
old kind has to be rewritten.

| 26.3 resource     | 26.4 resource                      | Notes                                                                                 |
|-------------------|------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `VolumeMigration` | `PersistentVolumeOps`              | Cluster-scoped, because a `PersistentVolume` is. Action `Migrate`.                    |
| `BackupRestore`   | `StorageBackupOps`                 | Absorbed as `spec.action: Restore`, the kind's only action.                           |
| `BackupPolicy`    | `StorageBackupPolicy`              | Selects its claims by label instead of a per-claim annotation.                        |
| `BackupImport`    | Retired                            | The backup store is the inventory, so a backup another cluster wrote needs no import. |
| `StorageNodeSet`  | `StorageCluster.spec.storageNodes` | The fleet template. The workers move to `ClusterDeploymentConfig`.                    |
| `Task`            | `StorageCluster.status.tasks`      | Canceled with a `StorageClusterOps` carrying `action: CancelTask`.                    |

### StorageCluster

| 26.3 property                                      | 26.4 property                                     | Notes                                           |
|----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| `spec.maxHugePagesSize`                            | `spec.minHugePagesSize`                           | The value is a minimum and always was.          |
| `spec.hashicorpVaultSettings.baseURL`              | `spec.kms.vault.endpoint`                         |                                                 |
| `spec.backup.localEndpoint`                        | `spec.backup.endpoint`                            | `bucket`, `prefix`, and `region` are added.     |
| `spec.openShiftCluster`                            | `spec.storageNodes.openshift`                     |                                                 |
| `spec.storageNodes.openShiftMachineConfigPool`     | `spec.storageNodes.openshift.machineConfigPool`   |                                                 |
| `spec.enableDataRealignment`                       | `spec.disableDataRealignment`                     | **Inverted.** Realignment is on by default now. |
| `spec.volumeAutoPlacement.enabled`                 | `spec.enableVolumeAutoPlacement`                  | Moves up to the cluster spec.                   |
| `spec.volumeAutoPlacement.migrationEnabled`        | `spec.volumeAutoPlacement.disableMigration`       | **Inverted.**                                   |
| `spec.volumeAutoPlacement.latencyBenchmarkEnabled` | `spec.volumeAutoPlacement.enableLatencyBenchmark` |                                                 |
| `spec.volumeMigrationSettings.enabled`             | Removed                                           | Migration cannot be turned off.                 |
| `spec.action`                                      | `StorageClusterOps`                               |                                                 |
| `status.actionStatus`                              | `StorageClusterOps.status`                        |                                                 |

An inverted field is the dangerous row of this release. A spec that still carries `enableDataRealignment` or
`migrationEnabled` is accepted by the API server and ignored, and the feature runs with the opposite default.

### StorageClusterOps

| 26.3 property                     | 26.4 property           |
|-----------------------------------|-------------------------|
| `spec.nodeRollingRestart`         | `spec.rollingRestart`   |
| `status.nodeRollingRestartStatus` | `status.rollingRestart` |
| `status.triggered`                | Removed                 |

The action `node-recycle` is renamed to `RollingRestart`, and `activate`, `expand`, `shutdown`, `start`, and
`restart` become `Activate`, `Expand`, `Shutdown`, `Start`, and `Restart`. `CancelTask` is added.

### StorageNode

| 26.3 property                   | 26.4 property                                                 | Notes                                                    |
|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `spec.storageNodeSetRef`        | `spec.clusterRef` and `spec.nodeSet`                          | The node is owned by its cluster.                        |
| `spec.socketIndex`              | `spec.slot`                                                   |                                                          |
| `spec.overrides`                | `spec.config`                                                 |                                                          |
| `config.failureDomain`          | `config.failureDomain`                                        | Was an integer index, is a label value such as `rack-a`. |
| `spec.skipKubeletConfiguration` | `StorageCluster.spec.storageNodes.enableKubeletConfiguration` | **Inverted**, and per cluster.                           |
| `overrides.enableCpuTopology`   | `StorageCluster.spec.storageNodes.enableCpuTopology`          | Per cluster, not per node.                               |

### StorageNodeOps

| 26.3 property            | 26.4 property                   | Notes                                |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| `spec.storageNodeRef`    | `spec.nodeRef`                  |                                      |
| `spec.targetWorkerNode`  | `spec.migrate.targetWorkerNode` |                                      |
| `spec.newSsdPcie`        | `spec.migrate.newSsdPcie`       |                                      |
| `spec.drain`             | `spec.remove`                   | Matches the action it parameterizes. |
| `status.subPhase`        | `status.step.state`             |                                      |
| `status.volumesMigrated` | `status.drain.volumesMigrated`  |                                      |
| `status.volumesPending`  | `status.drain.volumesTotal`     | A total instead of a remainder.      |
| `status.triggered`       | Removed                         |                                      |

The six actions become `Shutdown`, `Restart`, `Suspend`, `Resume`, `Remove`, and `Migrate`, and
`HostMaintenance` is added. The sub-phases `Migrating` and `Restarting` of a migration become the steps
`Relocating` and `AwaitingNode`, and the `Migrating` sub-phase of a removal becomes `MigratingVolumes`.

### StoragePool

| 26.3 property                                       | 26.4 property                                   |
|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| `spec.clusterName`                                  | `spec.clusterRef`                               |
| `spec.capacityLimit`                                | `spec.limits.capacity`                          |
| `spec.logicalVolumeMaxSize`                         | `spec.limits.maxVolumeSize`                     |
| `spec.qos.iops`                                     | `spec.limits.iops`                              |
| `spec.qos.throughput`                               | `spec.limits.throughput`                        |
| `spec.dhchap`                                       | `spec.volumeDefaults.enableDHCHAP`              |
| `spec.storageClassParameters.qosRwIops`             | `spec.volumeDefaults.iops`                      |
| `spec.storageClassParameters.qosRwMbytes`           | `spec.volumeDefaults.throughput.readWrite`      |
| `spec.storageClassParameters.qosRMbytes`            | `spec.volumeDefaults.throughput.read`           |
| `spec.storageClassParameters.qosWMbytes`            | `spec.volumeDefaults.throughput.write`          |
| `spec.storageClassParameters.encryption`            | `spec.volumeDefaults.enableEncryption`          |
| `spec.storageClassParameters.maxNamespacePerSubsys` | `spec.volumeDefaults.maxNamespacesPerSubsystem` |
| `spec.storageClassParameters.fabric`                | `spec.volumeDefaults.fabric`                    |
| `spec.storageClassParameters.filesystem`            | `spec.volumeDefaults.filesystem`                |
| `spec.storageClassParameters.tune2fsReservedBlocks` | `spec.volumeDefaults.tune2fsReservedBlocks`     |
| `spec.action`, `spec.status`                        | Removed                                         |

`spec.limits` is mutable, so a capacity or a QoS ceiling is raised on a running pool. `spec.volumeDefaults` is
immutable, because the parameters of the generated `StorageClass` are.

### StorageBackup, StorageBackupPolicy, and PersistentVolumeOps

| 26.3 property                         | 26.4 property                                    | Notes                                                |
|---------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `StorageBackup.spec.clusterName`      | `spec.clusterRef`                                |                                                      |
| `StorageBackup.spec.pvcRef`           | Removed                                          | The kind is discovered from the store, not authored. |
| `StorageBackup` flat status fields    | `status.backup` and `status.source`              | The copy and the volume it was taken from.           |
| `BackupPolicy.spec.clusterName`       | `StorageBackupPolicy.spec.clusterRef`            |                                                      |
| `BackupPolicy.status.attachedLvols`   | `StorageBackupPolicy.status.attachedClaims`      |                                                      |
| `VolumeMigration.spec.pvName`         | `PersistentVolumeOps.spec.persistentVolumeName`  |                                                      |
| `VolumeMigration.spec.targetNodeUUID` | `PersistentVolumeOps.spec.migrate.targetNodeRef` | Names a `StorageNode` object, not a UUID.            |
| `VolumeMigration` phase `Completed`   | `PersistentVolumeOps` phase `Succeeded`          |                                                      |

### ControlPlane

| 26.3 property | 26.4 property             | Notes                                                       |
|---------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `spec.image`  | `spec.source.local.image` | `spec.source.managed` names a remote control plane instead. |
| phase `Ready` | phase `Available`         | `Degraded` and `Unavailable` are added.                     |

### StorageClass Parameters and Claim Annotations

The QoS keys are renamed outside the CRD schemas as well. Every generation is read, because the parameters of a
`StorageClass` cannot be changed after it is created, so a class an older release generated keeps working.

| 26.3 parameter  | 26.4 parameter             | 26.4 claim annotation                             |
|-----------------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `qos_rw_iops`   | `max_iops`                 | `storage.simplyblock.io/max-iops`                 |
| `qos_rw_mbytes` | `max_mbytes_per_sec`       | `storage.simplyblock.io/max-mbytes-per-sec`       |
| `qos_r_mbytes`  | `max_read_mbytes_per_sec`  | `storage.simplyblock.io/max-read-mbytes-per-sec`  |
| `qos_w_mbytes`  | `max_write_mbytes_per_sec` | `storage.simplyblock.io/max-write-mbytes-per-sec` |

A `StorageClass` is assigned to a storage pool by three labels, `storage.simplyblock.io/namespace`,
`storage.simplyblock.io/cluster`, and `storage.simplyblock.io/pool`, instead of being named after the pool. A pool
may have any number of classes. The parameter `dhchap_node_label` is renamed to `dhchap_node_selector`, and the
node label it names changes from `simplyblock.io/pool.<namespace>.<cluster>.<pool>` to
`storage.simplyblock.io/storage-pool.<pool-uuid>`.

## Upgrade Considerations

- TODO, to be confirmed once the `simplyblock-upgrade` tool is released.

## Known Issues

- TODO, to be re-checked against the 26.3 known issues.

## Features to Expect with Next Major Release

- The ability to use different erasure coding schemas within the same cluster.
- Inline data integrity validation to prevent silent data corruption.

<!-- source: https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/release-notes/26-3/ -->

# 26.3

Simplyblock is happy to release Simplyblock 26.3. The changes are grouped by the component they belong to: the
simplyblock control plane and storage plane, and the Kubernetes components, meaning the Simplyblock Operator and
Simplyblock CSI.

## Simplyblock

The control plane and the storage plane are released together and share a version number. The changes below apply
to every deployment, including a Kubernetes-based one.

### New Features

- **Control Plane:** Added asynchronous replication between two storage clusters. Several destinations per cluster
  are supported, the cadence and the retention are set per replication policy, and a failover is requested for a
  single volume, a whole policy, or a whole destination.
- **Control Plane:** Added the planned cross-cluster cutover, by which a volume is handed over to another cluster
  under control. The remaining delta is shrunk, the source is fenced, and the client is moved to the target. The
  return to a recovered source runs as a delta, and the return to a fresh cluster as a full copy.
- **Control Plane:** Added support for failure domains. Data chunks, parity chunks, journal copies, and the
  secondary and tertiary nodes are spread across distinct domains, with a host-disjoint fallback and a warning
  where that is not possible.
- **Control Plane:** Added online storage node removal, which runs as a resumable background task and re-hosts the
  replicas and devices the node holds, and the expansion of an FTT 2 cluster by a single node. Several nodes are
  now added in parallel.
- **Control Plane:** Added cluster-wide maintenance operations. Every node of a cluster is restarted in one step,
  and the creation, deletion, and modification of volumes, snapshots, clones, and pools is refused and resumed for
  the whole cluster. Read paths and the restarts, migrations, and repairs a cluster performs on itself are
  unaffected.
- **Control Plane:** Added release-specific upgrade plug-ins, which run their preparation step before a cluster
  update and their completion step after it, and record the installed release on the cluster.
- **Control Plane:** Added batch migration of namespaced volumes, by which every volume that shares an NVMe-oF
  subsystem is moved as one coordinated group. What a failed migration left behind on the target is removed
  idempotently.
- **Control Plane:** Added quorum-based device exclusion. A device that draws I/O errors from a quorum of the other
  online nodes is excluded cluster-wide, independent of what its NVMe controller reports, which is the case a
  slow-but-connected device previously slipped through. A device whose latency deviates from the cluster average is
  reported as a warning event before it fails.
- **Control Plane:** Added alerting from the cluster event log, which provisions Grafana rules that read the
  transition an entity made rather than the state it ended in. Journal events are now collected into the event log
  next to the distrib events.
- **Control Plane:** Added a FoundationDB exporter with its own dashboard, request metrics of the management API,
  the device health information the storage plane holds, and a retention period of 30 days for cluster tasks and
  their logs.
- **Control Plane:** Added a rebalance operation to the cluster API, validation of the erasure coding scheme by the
  management API, and independent NVMe device filters for a storage node, where the device model and the size range
  are accepted alone as well as together.
- **Storage Plane:** The journal device of a node is now a RAID 0+1 stack instead of an N-way mirror across the
  journal partition of every drive. Write amplification is capped at two physical writes per journal record and per
  node, independent of the drive count, and a drive lifecycle event rebuilds the affected leg instead of the whole
  mirror.
- **Storage Plane:** Added a second generation of distrib write protection. A new cluster is created on it, and an
  upgraded cluster is moved over once every online node has migrated. An offline node is brought over by its next
  restart.
- **Storage Plane:** The ANA state change of a volume is now scoped to its namespace instead of the whole
  subsystem. A volume that shares its subsystem with other volumes is failed over, suspended, and migrated without
  moving their I/O to the other node.
- **Storage Plane:** The core allocation of a storage node gives the distrib and poller threads their share before
  alceml, which takes its device-scaled count from what is left. Explicit layouts are added for hosts with two to
  five vCPUs.
- **General:** Added diagnostics for a latency or crash investigation: the bdev latency histograms with a per-layer
  probe, by which a tail-latency spike is localized to a layer of the bdev stack, and the host directory
  `/var/crash` mounted into the storage plane container, so that a core dump survives the container.
- **General:** Updated the packages inherited from the container base images and dropped `wget` from the image, to
  resolve open CVEs.

### Fixes

- **Control Plane:** Fixed the loss of I/O during a storage node restart, where an unbounded operation inside the
  port fence could outlast the client keep-alive.
- **Control Plane:** Improved the recovery of a cluster after a full reboot. An activation that wedged is detected
  by a watchdog, automatic reactivation is gated on every node being online, and a suspended cluster is drained to
  all-offline before it is restarted.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed storage nodes flapping to the down state on a health probe timeout, and a node that is
  down no longer counts toward the suspension of the cluster. The suspension is gated on an actual loss of the data
  plane rather than on an unreachable management network.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed three ways in which a highly available volume could silently lose one of its paths, and
  the duplicate paths a repair left behind are now pruned. No leadership over an lvstore is granted while a restart
  or a recovery task owns the movement of it.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the failover of a namespaced volume, which the kernel rejected with mismatching
  identifiers.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the deletion pipeline of volumes and snapshots. A delete the cluster cannot complete is
  refused rather than accepted, a deferred delete completes once the node it waited for returns, and concurrent
  operations on one snapshot chain are mutually exclusive, which closes a corruption of the blob tree.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the migration of a volume whose snapshot chain spans several nodes, of an encrypted
  volume, and of a volume with a tertiary node. A migration whose source node goes offline is suspended instead of
  being cleaned up on the target.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the replication of the blob chain of a volume, which replicated only the snapshots of the
  volume itself. A failover only ever targets a fully replicated and live snapshot, and a replication no longer
  halts silently under back-pressure.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the addition of a storage node, which aborted on a lock timeout, on a stale in-creation
  record, or on an already provisioned device slot, and which did not survive the CPU topology reboot. A re-entry
  is idempotent now, and the status of a node, a device, a cluster, and a volume is written through a
  compare-and-set operation, so that a crashed writer cannot leave a stale status behind.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the capacity reporting, which mixed raw with effective capacity, and the cluster
  admission check, which did not count the utilization of snapshots. On a storage pool, the capacity check of a
  resize no longer counts the volume being resized twice.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the cloning of an encrypted volume, for which the crypto layer was missing from the
  recorded bdev stack, the key management of the local KMS, and the rendering of secrets in the management API.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed a forced storage node shutdown that could block indefinitely, a cluster that grew by
  being reactivated, a cluster expansion that did not reattach the sibling failover of its donor node, and the
  leases of long-running tasks, which expired while the task was still running.
- **Control Plane:** Improved the throughput of the snapshot and volume monitors, which process chains and nodes in
  parallel, and the logging to Graylog, which is written non-blocking, so that a slow log target no longer holds up
  the control plane.
- **Storage Plane:** Improved the reliability of the graceful startup and the graceful shutdown of the storage
  plane. A storage plane whose RPC endpoint hangs on a live process is aborted instead of being waited for, and the
  wait for the journal replication of a peer is bounded, so that it cannot defer a restart indefinitely.
- **Storage Plane:** Fixed the roles of the hub volumes, which are active on both sides within a node and passive
  between nodes, and the hub volume subsystem, which was lost across a restart.
- **Storage Plane:** Fixed the re-admission of the devices of a node recovering from an outage, which was silently
  refused while the node had not yet reached the online state. The memory footprint of a node improved as well,
  since the small I/O buffers are sized from the subsystem count of the cluster.

### New Features in 26.3.1

- **Control Plane:** Added the alerts endpoint, `GET /api/v2/clusters/<CLUSTER_UUID>/alerts/`, which returns the
  conditions that currently need an operator.
- **Control Plane:** Added hard per-object limits, enforced on every create and resize: 70 TiB per volume, 100
  snapshots per volume, and 500 clones per snapshot. See [Limits](../reference/limits.md).
- **Control Plane:** The shared NVMe-oF subsystems of a storage node are aligned with the storage pools, so that a
  subsystem carries the namespaces of exactly one pool.
- **Control Plane:** Added the self-repair of a device left `unavailable` or `removed`, unless it was removed by the
  operator.
- **Control Plane:** Added the Grafana rule `API_request_latency_high`, which fires when the mean request latency of
  the control plane API stays above 15 seconds.

### Fixes in 26.3.1

- **Control Plane:** Fixed the client I/O errors during the restart of a primary storage node, where a non-leader peer
  kept accepting I/O through a half-demoted lvstore.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the loss of the last usable path on a graceful shutdown, where the hublvol controller of a
  secondary or tertiary node was detached along with it.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the `Invalid Namespace or Format` error a client received from a subsystem that became
  reachable before its namespaces were attached.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the silent partial registration of the volume subsystems during an lvstore rebuild.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed a volume deletion that stalled after its data had been freed, because the lvstore
  leadership moved while the asynchronous delete was running.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the journal geometry across an upgrade, where an existing journal could be rebuilt under
  the newer RAID layout.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the silent acceptance of a storage plane that was started without the NVMe options of the
  control plane.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the admission of a snapshot, which did not charge the utilized size of its source volume
  against the storage pool and the cluster.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the upgrade of a storage node whose record still carries the legacy
  `lvstore_stack_secondary` and `lvstore_stack_tertiary` values.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the flooding of the cluster event log with journal compression events, of which only a
  failure is persisted now.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the filesystem metrics of the node exporter, which were read from the wrong root path.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the handling of a FoundationDB backup, whose retention metadata was not recorded.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the log collection bundle, which aborted in Docker mode on a missing kubeconfig.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed a fatal Python error at the shutdown of the storage node proxy, whose statistics thread
  outlived the interpreter.
- **Control Plane:** Fixed the log levels of the management API and of the Docker Swarm services.

## Kubernetes

The changes below apply to Kubernetes-based deployments only. They are delivered by the Simplyblock Operator and by
Simplyblock CSI.

### New Features

- **Operator:** Added support for failure domains, by which erasure coding chunks and failover paths are spread
  across racks or availability zones. Workers are assigned to a domain through the `StorageNodeSet`, and the
  effective domain of a worker is reflected in the status of the `StorageNode`.
- **Operator:** Added support for several `StorageNodeSet` resources per storage cluster, by which workers with
  different hardware or a different role are enrolled with their own configuration, and for the parallel addition
  of storage nodes.
- **Operator:** Added live volume migration through the new `VolumeMigration` resource, by which the backing
  logical volume is moved between storage nodes while the volume stays online. The new NVMe-oF paths on the target
  node are validated on every consuming worker before the migration is continued.
- **Operator:** Added the storage node drain, removal, and host migration workflows, requested with a
  `StorageNodeOps` resource. A removal suspends the node, migrates its volumes to the remaining nodes, verifies the
  result, and removes the node, and a migration relocates the identity of a storage node to a different worker.
- **Operator:** Added support for asynchronous replication between two storage clusters, declared with the new
  `ReplicationPair`, `ReplicationPolicy`, and `ReplicationSlot` resources. Failover and failback are requested with
  a `ReplicationOps` resource, scoped to a replication target, a policy, or a single volume, and a PVC is enrolled
  into a policy through an annotation.
- **Operator:** Added automatic, latency-based volume rebalancing and back storage data realignment, which are
  configured per cluster and triggered independently of each other.
- **Operator:** Added support for topology-aware provisioning across several storage clusters, by which a volume is
  provisioned in the cluster that matches the topology of the consuming workload, the option to skip the creation
  of the FoundationDB cluster, and the adoption of an existing Helm-deployed storage cluster, storage pool, and
  storage nodes into the operator resources.
- **Operator:** Added configuration of the image pull policy, the resource limits, and the SPDK system memory of
  the storage node workloads, and of a custom OpenShift `MachineConfigPool`, so that storage nodes are rebooted
  through a pool that is separate from the remaining workers. Every image reference is validated against the
  trusted registries, and a field that cannot be changed after creation is rejected instead of being ignored
  silently.
- **Operator:** The Thanos data of the monitoring stack is now stored in MinIO instead of a filesystem-backed
  object store, and Prometheus can be deployed with more than one replica.
- **CSI Driver:** Added support for co-locating the primary storage node of a volume with the worker that runs the
  consuming pod, and for the migration of namespaced volumes together with the coordinated restart of all pods that
  share an NVMe subsystem.
- **CSI Driver:** Added the detection and the repair of stale NVMe-oF subsystems and controllers on a worker.
- **CSI Driver:** The presence of a device is registered when the volume is connected, instead of only by polling,
  and the host NQN and the DH-CHAP secrets are forwarded at that point.

### Fixes

- **Operator:** Fixed the release of the NVMe target paths of a migration that never reaches its cutover, and the
  rebuild of the storage node configuration after an operator restart with an in-flight storage node migration.
- **Operator:** Fixed the `StoragePool` resource remaining in `Terminating` when its backend UUID was never set,
  and the PVC validator, which did not accept all of the volume placement annotations.
- **CSI Driver:** Fixed incompatibilities when formatting and mounting ext4 and XFS volumes, and the connection of
  a volume in a cluster with more than one storage pool.
- **CSI Driver:** Fixed the loss of the kernel module configuration on the host, which was written into the
  ephemeral filesystem of the storage node container and was gone after the CPU topology reboot during a node
  addition.
- **CSI Driver:** Fixed the restart loop of the CSI controller container, caused by dangling snapshots and volumes
  of a removed cluster. A gRPC keepalive and a connection timeout now detect a broken connection to a control
  plane instead of blocking a request.
- **Operator and CSI Driver:** Updated the container base images and the Go dependencies to resolve open CVEs.

### Fixes in 26.3.1

- **Operator:** Fixed the deletion of a `StoragePool` with DHCHAP enabled, which stayed in `Terminating` because the
  update dropping its finalizer was rejected by its own validation.
- **Operator:** Fixed the creation of a `StoragePool` with DHCHAP enabled and an empty `allowedNodes`, which is
  rejected now, since such a pool can never provision a volume.
- **Operator:** Fixed the generated `StorageClass` of a DHCHAP pool, whose `allowedTopologies` term matched no node.
- **Operator:** Fixed the label marking the allowed nodes of a `StoragePool`, which is keyed by the pool UUID now and
  can no longer exceed the 63 bytes a label name allows.
- **Operator:** Fixed the failback of a replicated volume, whose target cluster, pool, and volume were not resolved
  through the relationship lookup.
- **Operator:** Fixed the list of owned custom resource definitions in the cluster service version.
- **Operator:** Updated `golang.org/x/crypto` and the etcd client to resolve three high severity advisories.
- **CSI Driver:** Fixed the connection monitor, whose repair pass tore down a path that its reconcile pass had created
  moments earlier.

## Important Changes

- The storage plane sizing of a node moves to the cluster. The flags `--max-subsys`, `--hugepages-mem`, and
  `--vcpu-count` are set on `sbctl cluster create` and `sbctl cluster add`, and a node adopts them
  when it is added and on every restart. `--max-subsys`, `--max-size`, and `--cores-percentage` are removed from
  `sbctl storage-node configure`, and `--max-subsys` and `--max-size` from
  `sbctl storage-node restart`. The flag `--max-lvol` is renamed to `--max-subsys`, which is what it has
  always limited.
- The core budget of the storage plane is an absolute vCPU count instead of a percentage. A node that cannot satisfy
  the count of its cluster, plus one core for the system, is refused instead of running on fewer cores than
  requested. `sbctl cluster update --vcpu-count` does not exist, because rewriting the core mask of every
  node belongs to a deliberate redeployment.
- A configured subsystem limit above 75 per storage node is rejected, where it was accepted and then clamped
  silently before, so a node reserved huge pages for subsystems it could never serve. An lvstore serves at most 6000
  objects, counting volumes, clones, and snapshots, and a create beyond that limit is refused.
- Failure domains are a deploy-time feature. A cluster cannot be upgraded into them, and `--enable-failure-domain`
  has to be set at creation time. Once it is set, `--failure-domain` is mandatory on every
  `sbctl storage-node add-node` and rejected on a cluster without the feature.
- `sbctl storage-node remove` no longer migrates the data of the node. The node has to host no volumes and no
  snapshots, and those are migrated beforehand. The flag `--force-remove` no longer removes volumes and snapshots,
  it cancels the active tasks of the node before the removal starts.
- The commands `sbctl storage-node resume`, `sbctl storage-node get-bdevs`, and
  `sbctl storage-node unload` are removed. Instead of `resume`, `sbctl storage-node restart` has to
  be used.
- The command `sbctl cluster add-replication` is deprecated. Instead, the commands
  `sbctl cluster replication-target-add` and `sbctl cluster replication-policy-add` have to be used,
  which support more than one destination per cluster.
- `sbctl volume migrate` only pre-creates the target subsystem and returns the migration id and the NVMe
  connect strings. The flags `--deadline` and `--max-retries` move to `sbctl volume migrate-continue`, which
  advances the migration once the client is connected.
- After `sbctl cluster update`, two commands have to be run. `sbctl cluster upgrade-complete`
  releases the journal compression hold the update took across its rolling restart and records the installed
  release, and `sbctl cluster switch-write-protection` moves the cluster to the second generation of distrib
  write protection, on which it does not land by itself.
- The flag `--all` is removed from `sbctl snapshot list`, which gained `--lvol-id`, `--node-id`, and
  `--json`. The flag `--cluster-id` is removed from `sbctl backup restore`, whose cluster is derived from the
  backup.
- The `Pool` resource is renamed to `StoragePool`, and the resource enrolling a group of workers is renamed from
  `StorageNode` to `StorageNodeSet`. The name `StorageNode` is now used for the per-worker resource that is created
  by the operator.
- The field `maxLogicalVolumeCount` is renamed to `maxSubsystemCount`, and the field `corePercentage` is removed.
  Storage node sizing is moved from the `StorageNodeSet` to the cluster scope, and the field `partitions` is replaced
  by `enableJournalDevice`.
- The deprecated `StorageCluster` fields `blockSize`, `qpairCount`, `pageSizeInBlocks`, `maxQueueSize`,
  `inflightIOThreshold`, `strictNodeAntiAffinity`, `haType`, `isSingleNode`, and `clientQpairCount` are removed.
- The `StorageCluster` spec field `maxFaultTolerance` is replaced by `maxConcurrentWorkerRestarts`, which is capped
  at the fault tolerance of the cluster. The backend-reported `maxFaultTolerance` remains part of the status.
- The field `unpinBeforeDrain` is removed. A pinned volume has to be unpinned manually before its storage node is
  drained.
- The volume placement annotations are unified into `simplyblock.io/selected-storage-node`. On a new PVC, a host id
  supplied through `simplyblock.io/host-id` or `simplybk/host-id` is rewritten into that annotation and treated as a
  pin. On a pre-existing PVC, both legacy annotations are still honored as the lowest-priority source of the primary
  storage node.

## Upgrade Considerations

- The CSI driver added an extended check to prevent an accidental filesystem format onto an existing pre-formatted
  volume in one of the upstream CSI libraries. To ensure all existing volumes work as expected, users are highly
  encouraged to run this script after upgrading to 26.3.0. [Annotate existing PVCs Script](https://install.simplyblock.io/scripts/backfill-on-disk-filesystem.sh){:target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
- An upgrade from the previous R25 Helm chart to the R26 Operator installation requires a maintenance window and
  additional steps. See the [Upgrade Procedure R25 to R26](../upgrades/upgrade-notes-r25-r26.md) for details.

## Known Issues

- At the moment it is only possible to define one erasure coding schema per cluster.
- When deleting pods with simplyblock-backed PVCs, it is important to delete the pod first, before deleting the PVC.

    ```bash title="Deleting a pod before its persistent volume claim"
    kubectl delete pod <pod-name> --wait=true
    kubectl delete pvc <pvc-name> --wait=true
    ```

- A full FTT 1 or FTT 2 network outage can create a situation where surviving nodes lose access to the last journal
  records. This can cause loss of I/O availability until at least one node is restarted.
- Node Removal currently only works with online nodes.

## Features to Expect with Next Major Release

- The ability to use different erasure coding schemas within the same cluster.
- Inline data integrity validation to prevent silent data corruption.

# 26.2-PRE

Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 26.2-PRE.

## New Features

- Storage Plane: Added support for DH-CHAP and transport layer security (TLS) for the storage plane and communication between NVMe targets and initiators.
- Storage Plane: Added support volume backup and restore. The new mechanism takes backups of snapshots and sends the snapshot-chains to an S3-compatible storage. Backup retention, merge policies, and auto-backup schedules are configured via the operator. Snapshots can be restored into volumes (PVCs) on the same cluster or into a different cluster. Backup is storage-efficient (delta-only, compressed).
- Storage Plane: Added support for remote snapshot replication. Snapshots can be asynchronously replicated btw. nodes and sites in a network-efficient manner.
- Storage Plane: Added support for asynchronous replication which adds the ability to automatically failing-over and failing-back of selected volumes across sites with a certain time-gap/backlog (e.g., 5 minutes). This is useful for slow links and provides significantly better RTO (zero) and RPO (minimum: 1 minute) than traditional backups.
- Storage Plane: Added support for FTT 2 (failure to tolerate) which enables up to two failover paths. When enabled, simplyblock creates three communication paths between the initiators and the NVMe targets (primary, secondary, and tertiary) with identical subsystems able to process I/O. This allows the loss or maintenance of any two nodes in the cluster, regardless of the combination, at a point in time.
- Storage Plane: Added support for full multipathing within the storage cluster and between initiators and NVMe targets. This means that clients can have four (FTT=1) or six (FTT=2) connections via separate VLANs using separate networking paths. Each endpoint-combination uses two separate connections through the available network paths. It has advantages over simple bonding and multi-chassis link aggregation groups (MLAG).
- Kubernetes: Added support for OpenShift-managed TLS certificates for communication within the control plane and cluster endpoints.
- Kubernetes: Added support for mutual TLS (mTLS) on the control plane, using cert-manager-issued certificates.
- Kubernetes: Added support for offloading volume encryption keys to an external KMS (HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao).
- Kubernetes: Added support for namespaced volumes, which auto-create subsystems and namespaces within those subsystems in a pre-defined ratio (e.g., 8 or 16 namespaces per subsystem) in Kubernetes-based environments. The ratio can be configured via the operator.
- Kubernetes: Added a new, experimental Kubernetes operator to simplify the deployment of simplyblock control planes, storage planes, and the CSI driver in Kubernetes-based environments, such as OpenShift and Talos.
- General: All container images are now based on RHEL 10 base images and use Python 3.12. This solves multiple open CVEs and additional vulnerabilities.

## Fixes

No major fixes.

## Important Changes

- The command `sbctl storage-node suspend` has been deprecated and should not be used anymore. Use `sbctl storage-node shutdown` instead.
- The command `sbctl storage-node resume` has been deprecated and should not be used anymore. Use `sbctl storage-node restart` instead.
- The parameters `--crypto-key1` and `--crypto-key2` have been deprecated and cannot be used anymore. Encryption keys are now handled through the KMS-based system.

## Upgrade Considerations

It is possible to upgrade from `26.1` and `25.10.5`.

## Known Issues

- At the moment it is only possible to define one erasure coding schema per cluster.
- When deleting pods with simplyblock-backed PVCs, it is important to delete the pod first, before deleting the PVC.

  ```bash
  kubectl delete pod <pod-name> --wait=true
  kubectl delete pvc <pvc-name> --wait=true
  ```

## Features to Expect with Next Major Release

- The ability to use different erasure coding schemas within the same cluster.
- A significant performance optimization during node outages (journal writes).
- The ability to live migrate volumes between storage clusters.
- Inline data integrity validation to prevent silent data corruption.
- Support for failure domains, spreading data, journal copies, and failover paths across racks, cabinets, or availability zones.

# 25.10.5

Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 25.10.5.

## New Features

- Storage Plane: Storage nodes and storage clients (via the `nvme connect` command) can now be force-bound to a specific network interface on their host.
- Control Plane: The requirement for a route between the control plane nodes and storage plane nodes on the data network interface has been removed.
- Control Plane: The simplyblock cluster can now be configured with variable port ranges to allow for mitigation of port collisions on specific environments (mostly hyper-converged).
- Control Plane: The activation speed of large clusters and storage nodes has been improved by parallelizing internal state creation.
- Control Plane: The restart performance of large clusters has been improved by parallelizing reconnection to other storage nodes.
- Kubernetes: The CSI driver now automatically reconnects lost NVMe-oF connections on a multipathed logical volume as long as there is at least one healthy connection remaining.
- Kubernetes: The Kubernetes-based deployment now supports Kubernetes topology management.

## Fixes

- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where a new device on a storage node would disappear immediately after being added (`new` state)..
- Control Plane: Fixed multiple issues related to journaling and placement which could cause node-affinity issues, I/O interruptions, device formatting issues on 2+2 clusters after multiple 2-node outages in a row.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where multiple outages in a row could cause I/O interruptions.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where deleting a snapshot failed when the logical volumes' primary storage node had an outage.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where DPDK would fail to initialize in rare cases.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where deleting a logical volume failed when the logical volume's secondary storage node was in `down` state.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where the `--force` option would not work for the device removal.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where the `get-io-stats` command would return the same record for all rows.

## Upgrade Considerations

It is possible to upgrade from `25.10.4` and `25.10.4.2`.

## Known Issues

- At the moment, unnecessary retries of data migration occur while a storage node is down in m+2 schemas (2+2, 4+2). Data migration should pause once all migratable chunks that haven't been moved yet and resume once all nodes are online. Currently, it retries without success until all nodes are online. Which will be fixed as soon as possible.
- At the moment, sustaining full fault-tolerance requires more nodes than the theoretical minimum. This is due to a missing feature in the placement, which will be addressed as soon as possible.
- At the moment it is only possible to define one erasure coding schema per cluster.

## Features to Expect with Next Major Release

- The ability to use different erasure coding schemas within the same cluster.
- The ability to replicate snapshots to a foreign (remote) simplyblock cluster.
- The ability to asynchronously replicate volumes via snapshots in regular intervals and support fail-over in Kubernetes.
- The integration via a new Simplyblock Kubernetes Operator which uses CRDs to specify, create, and track a cluster, storage nodes, volumes, snapshots, and replications.
- A significant performance optimization during node outages (journal writes).
- The integration of cluster-internal multipathing for both RDMA- and TCP-based NVMe connections.
- The ability to send snapshot backups to remote S3-compatible storage.
- The ability to support multiple NVMe-oF failover connections with one primary and two secondary storage nodes for higher availability.

# 25.10.4

Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 25.10.4.

## New Features

- The storage node addition tasks (creating partitions and internal devices) are now performed in parallel.
- The cluster statistics are moved from FoundationDB to Prometheus to increase performance and reduce the memory footprint.
- The command `sbctl` now supports the `--version` (`-v) flag to display the version.
- The command `sbctl storage-node configure` now supports the `--force` flag to format NVMe devices whwn they are already formatted.
- The command `sbctl storage-node add-node` now supports the `--cores-percentage` flag to configure the percentage of cores to be used by the storage node (required on Oracle Linux).
- The command `sbctl storage-node add-node` now supports the `--nvme-names` flag to specify the NVMe device names.
- The command `sbctl storage-node add-node` now supports the `--format-4k` flag to format the NVMe devices with 4K alignment.
- The command `sbctl storage-node add-node` now supports the `--calculate-hp-only` flag to calculate the minimum required huge pages.
- The commands `sbctl cluster create` and `sbctl cluster add` now support the `--client-data-nic` flag to specify the client data network interface.
- The command `sbctl storage-node` now has additional subcommands to list snapshots and volumes by storage node.

## Fixes

- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where remote objects weren't correctly removed from the node on receiving distrib events.
- Control Plane: Improved communication between the control plane and spdk-proxy to avoid race conditions.
- Control Plane: Improved the reliability of logical volume deletions when multiple delete requests arrive simultaneously.
- Control Plane: Improved firewall rules management.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where pip packages were installed on cluster update.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue with the calculation of total_mem for multi storage nodes on the same NUMA node.
- Control Plane: Improved the reliability of device connections when storage nodes connect or disconnect.
- Control Plane: Improved the reliability of the cluster migration tasks.
- Control Plane: Improved the reliability of the cluster health checks.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where core isolation wouldn't correctly work on some systems.
- Control Plane: Improved the reliability of primary and secondary leader changes.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where additional delete operations would interfere with an asynchronous delete operation already in progress.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where failed devices couldn't be added back to the cluster.
- Control Plane: Improved the reliability of the storage node status update process.
- Control Plane: Improved the graceful startup and shutdown of the storage plane.
- Kubernetes: Fixed an issue where the wrong value was used to configure the hugepages.


## Upgrade Considerations

It is possible to upgrade from 25.10.3.

## Known Issues

Use of different erasure coding schemas per cluster is available but can cause I/O interrupt issues in some tests.
This feature is experimental and not GA.

# 25.10.2

Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 25.10.2.

## New Features

- Control Plane: The control plane can alternatively deploy into existing Kubernetes clusters
  and co-locate on workers with storage nodes.
- Kubernetes Support Matrix: Added OpenShift starting from version 4.19.0
- OpenStack driver: OpenStack driver is now available. It has support for most optional features
  and is tested from OpenStack 25.1 (Epoxy). On request, older versions of OS may be supported.
- The required memory footprint on storage nodes has been reduced from 0.2% of storage capacity to 0.05% of storage capacity.
- QoS: Pool-level QoS feature has been added.
- QoS Service Classes: A new feature to assign a service class to a volume. Service classes
  provide full performance isolation within the cluster.
- Support for flexible erasure coding schemas within a cluster.
- Support for RDMA fabric and mixed fabrics (RDMA, TCP)
- Some write performance improvements during first write to volume and node outage
- Support for namespace volumes. A single NVMe subsystem can expose up to 32 namespace volumes now

## Fixes

- Control Plane: Fixed a problem, which could lead to stuck deletes.

## Upgrade Considerations

It is possible to upgrade from 25.7.6 and 25.7.7. It is possible to add RDMA support for the fabric
during online upgrade.

## Known Issues

Use of different erasure coding schemas per cluster is available, but can cause I/O interrupt issues in some tests.
This feature is experimental and not GA.

# 25.6

Simplyblock is happy to release the general availability release of Simplyblock 25.6.

## New Features

Simplyblock strives to provide a strong product. Following is a list of the enhancements and features that made it into
this release.

- General: Renamed `sbcli` to `sbctl`. The old `sbcli` command is deprecated but still available as a fallback for scripts.
- Storage Plane: Increased maximum of available logical volumes per storage node to 1,000.
- Storage Plane: Added the option to start multiple storage nodes in parallel on the same host. This is useful for machines with multiple NUMA nodes and many CPU cores to increase scalability.
- Storage Plane: Added NVMe multipathing independent high-availability between storage nodes to harden resilience against network issues and improve failover.
- Storage Plane: Removed separate secondary storage nodes for failover. From now on, all storage nodes act as primary and secondary storage nodes.
- Storage Plane: Added I/O redirection in case of failover to secondary to improve cluster stability and failover times.
- Storage Plane: Added support for CPU Core Isolation to improve performance consistency. Core masks and core isolation are auto-applied on disaggregated setups.
- Storage Plane: Added `sbctl storage-node configure` command to automate the configuration of new storage nodes. See [the CLI reference](../reference/cli/index.md) for more information.
- Storage Plane: Added optimized algorithms for the 4+1 and 4+2 erasure coding configurations.
- Storage Plane: Reimplemented the Quality of Service (QoS) subsystem with significant less overhead than the old one.
- Storage Plane: Added support for namespaced logical volumes (experimental).
- Storage Plane: Reimplemented the initialization of a new page to significantly improve the performance of first write to page issues.
- Storage Plane: Added support for optional labels when using strict anti-affinity.
- Storage Plane: Added support for node affinity in case of a device failure to try to recover onto another device on the host.
- Proxmox: Added support for native Proxmox node migration.
- Talos: Added support to deploy on Talos-based OS-images.
- AWS: Added Bottlerocket support.
- AWS: Added multipathing support for Amazon Linux 2, Amazon Linux 2023, Bottlerocket.
- GCP: Added support for Google Compute Engine.

## Fixes

- Storage Plane: Fixed a critical issue on cluster expansion during rebalancing.
- Storage Plane: Optimized internal journal compression of meta-data to use fewer CPU resources.
- Storage Plane: Significantly improved the fail-back time in failover situations.
- Storage Plane: Fixed a CRC checksum error that occurred in rare situations after a node outage.
- Storage Plane: Fixed a conflict resolution issue with could lead to data corruption in failover scenarios.
- Storage Plane: Fixed a segmentation fault after resizing multiple logical volumes in a fast sequence.
- Storage Plane: Fixed data placement issues which could lead to unexpected I/O interruptions after a sequence of outages.
- Storage Plane: Reduced huge pages consumption by about 1.5x. Huge pages are automatically recalculated on node restart.
- Storage Plane: Fixed an RPC issue on clusters with eight or more storage nodes.
- Storage Plane: Fixed a race condition on storage node restarts or cluster reactivations.
- Storage Plane: Hardened a health-check issue which affected multiple services.
- Storage Plane: Improved shared buffers calculation on large storage nodes.
- Storage Plane: Fixed an issue in the metadata journal which could lead to a temporary conflict and I/O interruption on the fail-back of large logical volumes.
- Storage Plane: Fixed an issue where a storage node would stay unhealthy after a cluster upgrade.
- Storage Plane: Fixed an issue where the internal journal devices would fail to automatically reconnect after a cluster outage.
- Storage Plane: Fixed an issue where a restart of one storage node could lead to a crash on another storage node.
- Storage Plane: Fixed reattaching Amazon EBS volumes when migrating a storage node to a new host.
- Control Plane: Improved error handling on the internal controller code base.
- Control Plane: Fixed a range of false-positive detections that lead to unexpected storage node restarts or, in rare cases, cluster suspension.
- Control Plane: Cleaned up the API from unnecessary calls and fixed smaller response content issues.
- Control Plane: Improved handling of Graylog in case of primary management node failover.
- Control Plane: Fixed multiple issues regarding spill-over and outages in case of a management node disk running full.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where the generated logical volume connection string is missing the logical volume id in the NQN.
- Control Plane: Fixed multiple build issues with ARM64 CPUs.
- Control Plane: Fixed multiple issues when deleting logical volumes and snapshots which could lead to dangling garbage and inconsistencies.
- Control Plane: Fixed a primary storage node restart bug.
- Control Plane: Improved NVMe device detection by switching from serial number to PCIe address.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue, related to logical volume operations, where FoundationDB's memory consumption would continue to increase over time.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where migration tasks would stale with status `mig error: 8, retrying`.
- Control Plane: Improved observability by polling thread information from SPDK and store it in Prometheus.
- Control Plane: Improved the performance of parallel logical volume creations.
- Control Plane: Fixed data unit of read_speed in the Grafana cluster dashboard.
- Control Plane: Fixed an issue where the PromAgent image wouldn't be upgraded on a cluster upgrade.
- Kubernetes: Fixed an issue where the CSI driver would hang if it tries to delete a snapshot in error state.
- Kubernetes: Fixed hanging NVMe/TCP connections in the CSI driver on storage node restarts or failovers.
- Kubernetes: Fixed an issue with failing volume snapshots.
- Kubernetes: Improved the version pinning of required services.
- Kubernetes: Fixed an issue where NVMe/TCP connections in multipathing setups would be disconnected in the wrong order.
- Proxmox: Improved automatic reconnecting of volumes after storage node restarts and failovers.

## Important Changes

- Architecture: Separate secondary nodes have been removed as a concept. Instead, in a high-availability cluster, every deployed primary storage node also acts as a secondary storage node to another primary.
- Storage Plane: NVMe devices are now identified by their serial number to enable PCIe renumbering in case of changes to the system configuration.
- Firewall rules adjustment: An existing port range _TCP/8080-8890_ was changed to _TCP/8080-8180_. The firewall configuration and AWS Security Groups need to be adjusted accordingly.
- Firewall rules adjustment: An existing port range _TCP/9090-9900_ was changed to _TCP/9100-9200_. The firewall configuration and AWS Security Groups need to be adjusted accordingly.
- Firewall rules adjustment: A new port range _TCP/9030-9059_ was added. The firewall configuration and AWS Security Groups need to be adjusted accordingly.
- Firewall rules adjustment: A new port range _TCP/9060-9099_ was added. The firewall configuration and AWS Security Groups need to be adjusted accordingly.
- Firewall rules adjustment: An existing port _TCP/4420_ has been removed. The firewall configuration and AWS Security Groups need to be adjusted accordingly.
- Image registry: The image registry moved from Amazon ECR to DockerHub.

## Known Issues

Simplyblock always seeks to provide a stable and strong release. However, smaller known issues happen. Following up is
a list of known issues for the current simplyblock release.

- GCP: On GCP, multiple Local SSDs are connected as NVMe Namespace devices. There is a bug that prevents more than one Local SSD from being added to a storage node. For the time being, use one Local SSD per storage node. The storage node must be sized accordingly.

# 25.3-PRE

Simplyblock is happy to release the pre-release version of the upcoming Simplyblock 25.3.

!!! warning
    This is a pre-release and may contain issues. It is not recommended for production use.

## New Features

Simplyblock strives to provide a strong product. Following is a list of the enhancements and features that made it into
this release.

- High availability has been significantly hardened for production. Main improvements concern the support for safe and interruption free fail-over and fail-back in different types of outage scenarios. Those include: partial network outage, full network outage, host failure, container failure, reboots, graceful and ungraceful shutdowns of nodes. Tested for single und dial node outages.
- Multiple journal compression bugs have been identified and fixed.
- Multiple journal fail-over bugs have been identified and fixed.
- Logical volume creation, deletion, snapshotting, and resizing can now be performed via a secondary storage node (when the primary storage node is offline).
- The system has been hardened against high load scenarios, determined by the amount of parallel NVMe-oF volumes per node, the amount of storage and parallel I/O. Tested up to 400 concurrent and fully active logical volumes per node and u to 20 concurrent I/O processes per logical volume.
- Erasure coding schemes _2+1_, _2+2_, _4+2_, _4+4_ have been made power-fail-safe with high-availability enabled.
- System has been extensively tested outside of AWS with KVM-based virtualization and on bare-metal deployments.
- Significant rework of the command line tool `sbcli` to simplify commands and parameters and make it more consistent. For more information see [Important Changes](#important-changes).
- Support for Linux Core Isolation to improve performance and system stability.
- Added support for Proxmox via the simplyblock Proxmox integration.

!!! info
    This is a pre-release and many of those known issues are expected to be resolved with the final release.

- The control plane reaches a limit at around 2,200 logical volumes.
- If a storage node goes offline while a logical volume is being deleted, the storage cluster may keep some garbage.
- In rare cases, resizing a logical volume under high I/O load may cause a storage node restart.
- If a storage cluster reaches its capacity limit and runs full, file systems on logical volumes may return I/O errors.
- A fail-back after a fail-over may increase to >10s (with freezing I/O) with a larger number of logical volumes per storage node (>100 logical volumes).
- A fail-over time may increase to >5s (with freezing I/O) on large logical volumes (>5 TB).
- During a node outage, I/O performance may drop significantly with certain I/O patterns due to a performance issue in the journal compression.
- Journal compression may cause significant I/O performance drops (10-20s) in periodic intervals under certain I/O load patterns, especially when the logical volume capacity reaches its limits for the first time.
- A peak read IOPS performance regression has been observed.
- In rare cases, a primary-secondary storage node combination may get into a flip-flop situation with multiple fail-over/fail-back iterations due to network or configuration issues of particular logical volumes or clients.
- A secondary node may get stuck when trying to restart under high load (>100 logical volumes).
- Node affinity rules are not considered after a storage node migration to a new host.
- Return code of sbcli commands is always 0.

---

Simplyblock regularly provides new releases with new features, performance enhancements, bugfixes, and more.

This section provides detailed information about each simplyblock release, including new features, enhancements, bug
fixes, and known issues. Stay informed about the latest developments to ensure optimal performance and take full
advantage of simplyblock's capabilities.
